summary: Traffic Sentinel turns one fixed junction camera into time-stamped traffic events and a causal accident-risk curve: YOLO11 detections, a ByteTrack-style tracker, a scene model learned from the sample videos and one rule per event class, run inside the organisers' time budget on any machine by a time governor. On our own (draft) labels of the four samples it reaches Score A 0.35, up from 0.13 before tuning. The biggest lesson: with a macro-F1 over every predicted class, knowing which classes not to predict mattered as much as improving the ones we keep.
worked: Decoding only the reference frames (I/P) of the camera's 10-bit 4:2:2 stream: exactly the 10 fps Part A needs, 15-28% faster, and the only way to stay inside the budget on small CPUs.
A time governor that probes the machine per video, degrades quality step by step and returns partial events at a hard deadline instead of an empty score.
Judging failure_to_yield on the vehicle's whole box and one segment per pass: F1 0.08 -> 0.49 on our dev labels.

Scoring Part B by the deceleration needed to avoid a conflict (DRAC) between a moving vehicle and a road user whose paths meet, calibrated so normal traffic sits at 0.03-0.07 and only 1-2 moments per video reach 0.5.

A perturbation test (jittering detections like a different GPU would) that found exactly the events that differed between our GPU box and a T4, and led to hysteresis and ID-switch chaining for pedestrians.
didnt: near_miss, illegal_u_turn and stopped_vehicle: tracker ID swaps between overlapping cars and signal queues produced almost only false positives (0-1 true of 34 predicted), so we stopped predicting them.
Riders on scooters and bicycles are detected as 'person' and still cause some jaywalking false positives.
Classes that depend on the signal phase or lane rules (red_light, illegal_turn, legality of U-turns) cannot be verified from this camera: most signal heads face away from it.
A stored empty-road background for obstacles: the samples span daylight to dusk, and it flagged whole videos until we switched to each video's own median.
Our dev labels are drafted from rendered frames and still await a teammate's confirmation; the scores are in-sample.
next: A small learned classifier on track features (relative speed, heading change, box overlap) for accident and near_miss instead of thresholds.
A rider/pedestrian classifier: associate a 'person' with the two-wheeler under it over time rather than per frame.
A ground-plane homography so speeds and gaps are metric instead of box-size-normalised.
Confirm the dev labels with two annotators and report inter-annotator agreement next to the scores.
